diagnosis: For [2335,13279] at budget 5, the independently found CF2 support differs by one edge, raises J from approximately 0.4583 to 0.5122, repairs sufficiency and preserves necessity. The default nevertheless rejects it because deleted-class probability rises from approximately 0.00066 to 0.00948. This identifies an acceptance constraint, not proof that the CF2 edge was in the gradient shortlist.
change: Optional binary-monotone policy permits continuous confidence tradeoffs while requiring strict J improvement and no binary necessity/sufficiency regression. Same saliency initialization, gradient proposal mechanism, 12 additions, 3 removals, 8 steps, full-graph screening and serial rechecks. No CF2 support or edge is supplied to the search. Componentwise remains the default.
regression: Query [5425,10431] at budget 20 loses necessity relative to the componentwise terminal result. Each policy still satisfies non-regression relative to its own shared initial support. A weaker acceptance constraint does not imply a better greedy terminal support.
diagnostic_case_outcome: The ordinary binary-monotone search repairs sufficiency at all three budgets for [2335,13279], using supports different from the supplied-for-analysis CF2 result. The CF2 answer was not injected.
cost_scope: About 27 percent more proposals and measured search time, despite equal per-step and step-count caps. Single-run alternating policy order on a shared GPU. Excludes initialization and final external metric evaluation, so not an end-to-end or equal-actual-compute claim.
verification: Source hashes, initial-support replay, support sizes, every accepted strict objective gain, both binary guards and default continuous guards checked. Cross-baseline record audit passed. Full suite: 134 passed. The rerun componentwise control matches all 300 historical binary outcomes but 23 final supports differ; this is not a claim of bitwise search trajectory reproduction.
limitations: All 100 queries were previously inspected, and the policy was motivated by a failure in this set. This is development evidence requiring confirmation on other validation cohorts before selection. No uncertainty or universal-superiority claim. Relaxed acceptance does not retain continuous componentwise non-regression.
coarsening_scope: Both new variants are ungrouped. Improvements are evidence about acceptance constraints, not an independent benefit of graph coarsening.
next_gate: Run the frozen policy on different dataset/seed validation cohorts and compare actual cost as well as quality before any method promotion. Preserve the one observed regression and compare grouping separately.
manuscript: Added the acceptance-constraint limitation and updated XZ20. No empirical values, tables or figures changed; compiled and visually checked the affected page.
